The Philippines is currently implementing a medium-term Public Financial Management (PFM) reform agenda under the Public Financial Management Reforms Roadmap 2024–2028, developed pursuant to Executive Order No. 29 (June 1, 2023). Implementation is ongoing.

Status and scope: The roadmap organizes reforms across 11 strategic focus areas: (1) planning and budgeting linkage, (2) cash management, (3) public asset management, (4) accounting and auditing, (5) PFM capacity development, (6) digital PFM, (7) PFM policy and legal framework, (8) public procurement, (9) disaster risk reduction and management, (10) PFM for local government units, and (11) monitoring and evaluation for public expenditure.

Timelines: Main reform period is 2024–2028. Some reforms build on earlier initiatives that remain ongoing, including UACS, TSA, electronic payments, cash budgeting, and internal audit improvements.

Milestones achieved: Prior roadmaps and ongoing reforms have already delivered important milestones, including program expenditure classification and performance-informed budgeting, implementation of the Treasury Single Account, establishment of the Unified Accounts Code Structure (UACS), automation of various PFM functions, introduction of citizen and performance audits, establishment of a PFM competency framework, and conduct of capacity-building programs.

Milestones to achieve / current reform actions: Current priorities include developing and implementing the Budget and Treasury Management System (BTMS) as the interoperable core of the government’s IFMIS; establishing BTMS quality controls; sustaining the eGovPay platform for government payments and collections; implementing an integrated project monitoring and reporting system; establishing a PFM data management architecture and comprehensive data lake/warehouse; enacting the Progressive Budgeting for Better and Modernized Governance Bill and its IRR; creating the Office of the Comptroller General; and amending PD No. 1445 (Government Auditing Code).

Responsible agencies: The PFM Committee leads the roadmap. The Philippines is implementing ongoing reforms to strengthen and fully institutionalize its Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS). Implementation is already underway rather than at a purely design stage: the government has rolled out key building blocks since 2010, and Executive Order No. 29, s. 2023 directed the full adoption/implementation of IFMIS across government agencies. Under the Public Financial Management Reforms Roadmap 2024–2028, the main strategy is to develop and implement the Budget and Treasury Management System (BTMS) as the interoperable core of IFMIS, while linking existing stand-alone and legacy systems through APIs to reduce disruption.

Timelines: foundational reforms began in 2010; several roadmap reforms remained ongoing after 2016; the MOA on Budget Reforms in 2018 accelerated digital budgeting tools; EO No. 29 in 2023 renewed the mandate for full implementation; and the current reform roadmap covers 2024–2028.

Milestones achieved: rollout of key PFM digital components including the Unified Accounts Code Structure (UACS), Treasury Single Account (TSA), Online Submission of Budget Proposals System (OSBPS), Unified Reporting System (URS), and adoption of BTMS-related digital reforms. The government has also harmonized account codes and improved online, real-time budget and cash management processes.

Milestones to achieve: full government-wide IFMIS adoption; further BTMS development and quality controls; integration/harmonization of agency systems; establishment of PFM data management architecture and a comprehensive data lake/warehouse; and continued institutionalization through legislation such as the Progressive Budgeting for Better and Modernized Governance Bill.

Responsible agencies: Department of Budget and Management (DBM), Department of Finance (DOF), and Bureau of the Treasury (BTr), with Commission on Audit (COA) involved in the broader PFM framework.

Donor partners: the sources do not identify a dedicated IFMIS donor, but ADB and other development partners are supporting the wider PFM reform agenda, including PEFA-related policy actions and strengthening country systems.

The Philippines is implementing institutional capacity-building reforms under the Public Financial Management (PFM) Reforms Roadmap 2024–2028. The main reforms include: (1) strengthening the institutional framework for PFM capacity-building; (2) developing and implementing a comprehensive capacity-building program and rollout plan; (3) establishing a digital ecosystem for the management and rapid rollout of the Public Financial Management Competency Program (PFMCP); (4) developing e-learning materials and tutorials for capacity-building programs; and (5) reviewing and updating the current PFM Competency Program and curriculum framework.

Implementation status: These reforms are ongoing/planned under the 2024–2028 roadmap, with several high-priority activities already initiated in 2024. A PEFA-related report also notes that the government continues to enhance its PFM system through digitalization initiatives, policy revisions, and capacity-building programs.

Timelines: The overall reform period is 2024–2028. Specific milestones include stocktaking of institutional stakeholders, existing programs, resources, and coverage in 2024–2025 (Activity 33). The development of the comprehensive capacity-building program and rollout plan is stated to begin in 2024 and be implemented during the remainder of the roadmap period. Under the digital ecosystem reform, establishing a database of PFM practitioners is scheduled to start in 2024.

Milestones achieved / underway: The roadmap itself has been adopted and priority interventions have been identified. Capacity-building providers across government have already been mapped conceptually, and implementation of stocktaking, digital learner management elements, and rollout planning has begun.

Milestones to achieve: Complete stocktaking; finalize and roll out the comprehensive capacity-building plan; establish the digital ecosystem and practitioner database; expand e-learning materials and tutorials; and update the PFMCP curriculum to better develop reform leaders and support best-practice policies, processes, and systems.
